summary: NSRP 114G offered up to VND 40,500/kg; Korean/Chinese yarn ~40,000
Lotte raised PP yarn import offer to 1,330 USD/ton CIF, M9600 coating 1,430
ICIS Vietnam PP yarn/inj rose sharply on crude surge and China shutdowns
paras: According to ICIS assessments released on last week's final trading day, September 11, the average price level for PP yarn/injection in Vietnam last week stood at USD 1,235/tonne/CFR, up USD 25/tonne from the week before. Price levels for other PP grades in the region also rose.

Asian PP prices rose sharply last week, driven by escalating tensions in the Middle East that sent crude oil prices surging to their highest level since May 2026. Suppliers faced mounting cost pressure.

In China, some PP plants have had to shut down or plan to halt operations. Polyolefin inventories at major petrochemical producers such as Sinopec and PetroChina fell considerably. As September is the peak-demand season in China and domestic PP prices are on an upward trend, these suppliers held firm on export prices and were less willing to cut them.

Supply allocated for September in Southeast Asia remained scarce. Some suppliers switched to offering October cargoes, but buyers showed little interest in late-delivery orders, as they needed material urgently for production and were also concerned that prices could correct downward once US-Iran tensions ease.

Many downstream manufacturers still struggled to pass the added costs on to product prices and were considering cutting operating rates rather than producing finished goods at a loss. Resin inventories at some manufacturers were low, as they largely bought on an as-needed basis.

In Vietnam, today, September 14, the domestic PP market saw some traders continue to push offers for NSRP's PP 114G higher, to VND 40,500/kg including VAT; some other distributors offered it at VND 40,000/kg including VAT, about VND 500-1,000/kg higher than late last week. These offer levels were even higher than imported PP yarn/injection from certain Korean and Chinese origins.

For example, offer prices for PP yarn of Lotte and Hyundai (South Korea) origin were recorded at VND 40,000/kg including VAT in the north; Chinese-origin PP yarn/injection was offered at port at VND 38,500-39,000/kg including VAT for cargoes soon to arrive, equivalent to the import offer quotations updated last week…

In fact, on last week's final trading day, some traders tested new offer levels by raising offers for NSRP-, BSR- and Hyosung Vina-origin PP yarn/injection to VND 40,000/kg including VAT, in order to gauge market response. “Domestically sourced PP is in short supply; at present most traders have no stock committed for far-forward delivery and are mainly selling their remaining inventory for prompt delivery, hence the tendency to push prices up,” a source said.

For other PP grades and product lines, price trends were somewhat more stable on the first trading day of the new week. Offer levels for PP copolymer of various origins were commonly in the VND 40,000-41,000/kg including VAT range; PP Film/coating (white) and random grades of Thai and Korean origin… were commonly in the VND 41,000-42,500/kg including VAT range.

On imports, late last week South Korea's Lotte Chemical raised its PP yarn offer to Vietnam to USD 1,330/tonne/CIF and settled M9600 PP coating at USD 1,430/tonne/CIF. Most Chinese producers offered prompt-delivery cargoes at above USD 1,300/tonne/CIF. Meanwhile, Thailand's IRPC offered its 1102K and K1111 PP yarn/injection grades at USD 1,400/tonne/CFR HCMC, PP 1100RC at USD 1,450/tonne/CFR, and PP Film 1126NK at USD 1,490/tonne/CIF…

summary: Premium LLDPE (Qamar FD21HS, Sabic 218WJ) scarce, offered higher
Lotte HDPE yarn closed 1,300; US LDPE Film up to 1,400-1,420 USD/ton CIF
PE seen hard to cool in September as crude stays high, China restocks
paras: According to ICIS assessments released on last week's final trading day, September 11, the average price of LDPE Film in Vietnam last week was USD 1,375/tonne/CFR, down a slight USD 5/tonne from the week before; the average price of LLDPE Film was USD 1,205/tonne/CFR, also down a slight USD 5/tonne; HDPE Film held flat at USD 1,265/tonne/CFR; HDPE injection held flat at USD 1,165/tonne/CFR; and HDPE blow likewise held flat at USD 1,185/tonne/CFR.

PE assessments in Vietnam ranged from flat to slightly lower, mainly because the previous week's price increases had been too steep and no transactions had taken place. Across the wider region, however, PE offer prices last week in fact continued to rise, owing to limited supply and high crude oil prices. Downstream customers remained cautious and kept to a restrained buying strategy in the face of higher offers; most were turning to US cargoes scheduled for November delivery to secure more competitive prices. The widening gap between buyers' target prices and sellers' expectations continued to hamper negotiations.

In Vietnam, over the past weekend, some buyers successfully closed imports of Lotte's HDPE yarn at USD 1,300/tonne/CIF; Lotte's LLDPE Film and injection were both settled at USD 1,350/tonne/CIF. For Chinese material, oil-based LLDPE Film was commonly offered at USD 1,310-1,320/tonne/CIF Vietnam; STL raised its HDPE Film offer to USD 1,350/tonne/CIF but closed no deals…

For Southeast Asian material, PTT of Thailand's distributor — after selling a fairly large volume of LLDPE injection at USD 1,300/tonne/CIF and HDPE yarn/film at USD 1,350/tonne/CIF — halted sales at those levels from midweek. It offered LDPE Film 2426K at USD 1,520/tonne/CIF but subsequently closed no sales. The distributor of Malaysia's Petlin offered LDPE Film C150Y at USD 1,480/tonne/CIF early in the week, though it remains unclear whether any customer closed an import at this price, as the producer then paused its quotations…

For US material, PE offers to Vietnam were fairly plentiful but prices also climbed, with LDPE Film offered up to USD 1,400-1,420/tonne/CIF; various LLDPE Film grades offered at USD 1,170/tonne/CIF; and HDPE blow offered at USD 1,170-1,230/tonne/CIF…

Domestically, according to market sources, spot PE remained fairly scarce. This drove traders to push offers for “premium” LLDPE Film grades higher, to VND 42,000-43,000/kg including VAT, up a further VND 500-1,000/kg from late last week.

“At present, very few traders have Qamar's LLDPE Film FD21HS… or Sabic's 218WJ… available for prompt delivery to customers. Additive-containing LLDPE is sold out. Many buyers have had to source additive-containing Chinese LLDPE Film as a substitute to meet immediate production needs, so Chinese LLDPE Film has also been pushed up to around VND 40,000/kg including VAT,” a northern source said.

Similarly, LDPE and HDPE continued to see offer trends ranging from flat to edging up, even though price levels were considered already too high. LDPE Film had been pushed up to VND 44,000-46,000/kg including VAT depending on grade and supplier; offers for various HDPE grades ranged from VND 40,000-43,000/kg including VAT, nearly level with LLDPE…

Notably, a growing number of market participants believe PE prices will be hard to cool within September, as oil prices are anchored at high levels and imported cargoes arriving in late September will only be enough to fulfill orders from customers who had already contracted to buy.

“Demand in China will rise strongly between now and the end of September as buyers replenish inventories before the early-October holiday week; these suppliers are unwilling to lower their offers even though few Vietnamese buyers are accepting imports at current offer levels. At present, Chinese-origin LDPE Film is being offered by many producers at up to USD 1,700/tonne/CIF Vietnam, while STL's HDPE Film FS7000 is offered at USD 1,350/tonne/CIF with no lower bids accepted…,” a source analyzed.

summary: Formosa Taiwan PVC to Vietnam +10 USD to 860-870 USD/ton CIF
Taiyo TH1000 offered 850-860 CIF, up 100 USD month-on-month
South Asia PVC now 70-80 USD above SE Asia; regional offers keep rising
paras: The PVC price gap between South Asia (typified by India) and Southeast Asia has widened considerably, with South Asian prices USD 70-80/tonne higher, prompting suppliers to direct more offers to South Asia. Today, September 14, for example, one Chinese supplier offered oil-based PVC for export to India at up to USD 905/tonne/CIF, whereas its export price to Southeast Asia was only about USD 830/tonne/CIF; coal-based PVC export offers from China to India were around USD 830-840/tonne/CIF, while offers to Southeast Asia were only about USD 760-770/tonne/CIF…

In practice, import offer prices for PVC into Southeast Asia and Vietnam have continued to trend upward in recent weeks, though the pace of increase has been restrained by still-high domestic inventories and demand still in its low season. With imported offers showing signs of tightening further, PVC prices remain under upward pressure rather than cooling.

Last week, Formosa Taiwan's PVC offer to Vietnam rose USD 10/tonne to USD 860-870/tonne/CIF, for late-September delivery… Although the offer increased, it carries little significance, because in practice Formosa's offered volumes are very small. Sources said Formosa has three cracking furnaces but currently only one is in operation. Formosa's PVC output has therefore fallen sharply due to the feedstock shortage, with volumes only sufficient for domestic consumption. Replenishing the remaining feedstock supply will take considerable time.

Distributor Itochu offered TH1000 PVC from Japan's Taiyo, for October 2026 delivery to Vietnam, at USD 850-860/tonne/CIF, up USD 100/tonne from the previous month's price. Meanwhile, offers for SE950/SE1000 PVC from the US producer Shintech to Vietnam this week were reported at USD 770-780/tonne/CIF, up a further USD 10-20/tonne from the previous week, with the cargo expected to arrive in January 2027. Offers from China were not overly abundant…

As a result, PVC offer prices in Vietnam on last week's end-of-week trading day were pushed up strongly, despite “sluggish” consumption. The general price level of oil-based PVC was driven up to VND 24,000-25,000/kg including VAT; coal-based PVC was likewise pushed up to VND 23,000-24,000/kg including VAT. In the north, most sellers raised their offer prices for oil-based PVC products — covering both domestically sourced and imported material — to VND 24,300/kg including VAT and above…
Today, on the first trading day of the new week, PVC price levels were shored up, although trading has yet to show any improvement.
